China Wind Power’s Global Challenge

AJ Cortese

Gavekal Technologies: New Energy | 17 Aug 2026

Chinese wind turbine makers are champions at home but much less visible abroad than their peers in solar, EVs and batteries. One reason is that China’s domestic wind industry is not saddled with as much profit-destroying excess capacity as other cleantech sectors, so turbine makers can still make money at home. A bigger factor is that the project economics of wind power are unique. Chinese turbine makers’ lower prices are often not enough to offset their perceived lower quality of service, and higher financing costs because of their shorter reliability records. Ironically, the fast Chinese product cycles that give EV brands a competitive edge are a problem for turbine makers, because they make it harder to establish long reliability track records.
